prompt: Implement negative_lookup(entry, query, now) for one ordinary RFC-2308-style negative cache entry. Return exactly {'kind':None|'NXDOMAIN'|'NODATA','ttl':nonnegative_integer}; every miss returns None/0. entry may be None (always a miss), or a dictionary with kind ('NXDOMAIN' or 'NODATA'), negative_name (the absent terminal name), queried_name (original query name retained only as metadata), qtype, qclass, view, stored_at (integer seconds), soa_ttl and soa_minimum (nonnegative integer seconds). query contains name, qtype, qclass, and view. Names are absolute ASCII DNS names ending in a dot; compare names, type labels and class labels case-insensitively, but view IDs exactly. The supplied query name is the name being checked at this stage of resolution, possibly the terminal target after CNAME chasing; this function does not follow aliases. NXDOMAIN matches negative_name/class/view regardless of query type. NODATA additionally requires the same query type. Never key a terminal negative result by the metadata queried_name if it differs. The chosen initial ordinary lifetime is min(soa_ttl,soa_minimum), with no additional local cap. At now>=stored_at subtract elapsed age and return a hit only if the remaining lifetime is strictly positive and the key matches. Retention received with zero negative lifetime and use exactly at expiry are misses. Inputs are accepted authoritative negatives with their relevant SOA already identified; query types are ordinary terminal-record types such as A/AAAA/TXT. Do not infer nonexistence for descendants, perform serve-stale, restart the timer on lookup, mutate inputs, or retain state across calls. NODATA here is a cache-result label, not a DNS wire RCODE.

Implement dnssec_cache_gate(record, now), returning exactly {'accepted':bool,'cache_ttl':int}. record contains rrset_ttl, rrsig_ttl, original_ttl (nonnegative integer seconds), inception and expiration (ordinary nonwrapping integer times with inception<=expiration), and booleans algorithm_supported, key_trusted, metadata_ok, signature_ok. Those booleans are caller-supplied verification results: algorithm support, an authenticated applicable DNSKEY, matching required metadata, and cryptographic signature verification. This is an ordinary non-wildcard RRset with one candidate RRSIG; implementing cryptography, a chain builder, or full DNSSEC security classification is outside this task. Accept exactly when all four booleans are True and inception<=now<=expiration. Rejection returns cache_ttl=0. Acceptance returns the maximum permitted ordinary cache lifetime min(rrset_ttl,rrsig_ttl,original_ttl,expiration-now), with no extra local cap. At the exact expiration instant the current transaction can pass this inclusive validity gate but has cache_ttl=0. Inputs must remain unchanged and each call is independent.

Implement nat_trace(events, mapping_mode='eim', filter_mode='apdf', idle_timeout=5, external_ip='203.0.113.1', first_port=40000), returning one dictionary per event with exactly result, external, internal, live_ports. This is a deterministic UDP mapping/filter/timer component model with abstract integer clock ticks, not deployed RFC-4787 timer conformance: timeout values 0, 1 and the default 5 exercise algorithm boundaries and do not claim these are compliant real-world timeout seconds. Every event has type and nonnegative integer time, in nondecreasing order. Endpoints are two-element lists [canonical_IPv4_string,integer_UDP_port]. An outbound event contains internal and remote endpoints; an inbound event contains external destination and remote source endpoints; a tick event has only type/time. Mapping mode 'eim' keys by internal IP and port only; 'apdm' also keys by remote IP and port. A new binding gets the next monotonically allocated external port starting at first_port, never reused in this trace, at external_ip. Inputs keep allocations in the valid port range. Outbound records the contacted remote pair for that binding, refreshes its expiry to time+idle_timeout, and returns result='mapped', external=[external_ip,port], internal=None. Inbound first requires a live binding at that exact external IP/port, otherwise result='unmapped'. For a live binding, filter mode 'eif' permits every remote pair; 'apdf' permits only pairs previously contacted through that binding. Denial returns 'filtered'; success returns 'delivered' with the internal endpoint. All non-outbound external values are None; all non-delivered internal values are None. Incoming packets never refresh timers under this selected permitted policy. Remove bindings with expiry<=time before processing every event and again before recording its snapshot. A zero-timeout outbound can be translated/reported but leaves no surviving binding. tick returns result='tick'. live_ports lists sorted active external ports after processing. idle_timeout is a nonnegative integer, modes and inputs are valid, and endpoints/port allocation parameters are supplied explicitly. Do not mutate inputs or earlier snapshots, retain state between calls, use a real network, or model hairpinning, external-port reuse or extra firewall behavior.

Implement lease_state(request_sent, ack_received, lease_duration, now, t1=None, t2=None) for a point query of a DHCPv4 lease clock after a matching allocation or renewal ACK has been accepted. Inputs are finite seconds: request_sent>=0, request_sent<=ack_received<=now, and lease_duration>0. Infinite leases, OFFER-only configuration, DHCPINFORM, NAK handling, transaction validation, and fallback to an older lease are outside this component. Use request_sent as the lease epoch; ACK arrival does not extend the deadline. t1/t2 are optional offsets from that epoch; omitted offsets use nominal 0.5/0.875 times lease_duration with no jitter. Inputs guarantee 0<T1<T2<lease_duration after defaults. Return exactly {'t1_at':number,'t2_at':number,'expires_at':number,'phase':str,'usable':bool}. Deadlines are epoch plus their respective offsets/duration. At now>=expires_at return phase='INIT',usable=False; otherwise at now>=t2_at use 'REBINDING',True; otherwise at now>=t1_at use 'RENEWING',True; otherwise use 'BOUND',True. Apply already-overdue timers immediately in this point-query model. A delayed accepted ACK whose computed lease has already expired therefore returns INIT/unusable. Every call uses only its own accepted request/ACK clock data, including a new renewal epoch, with no retained call state or actual packet transmission.

Implement slaac_update(now, remaining_valid, advertised_valid, advertised_preferred, authenticated=False) for an existing SLAAC address under the ordered RFC-4862 lifetime-update rules. All times/durations are finite seconds: now>=0, remaining_valid>0, advertised_valid>=0, and 0<=advertised_preferred<=advertised_valid. The caller has already accepted the matching PIO (A set, non-link-local prefix and compatible prefix/IID lengths); this task does not model new-address formation, DAD, Router Lifetime, or rejected PIOs. Let R=remaining_valid and V=advertised_valid. If V>7200 or V>R, newR=V. Otherwise, if R<=7200, newR=V when authenticated=True and R otherwise. In the remaining branch newR=7200, including when authenticated=True. Independently set newP=advertised_preferred in every branch. Return exactly {'valid_remaining':newR,'preferred_remaining':newP,'valid_until':now+newR,'preferred_until':now+newP,'state':str}; state is 'invalid' if newR==0, otherwise 'deprecated' if newP==0, otherwise 'preferred'. Authentication changes only the stated second branch, not the entire ordered algorithm. Each call is independent and reports the immediate update without advancing a later timer; no infinity sentinel is used.
